essence: Armilla has no walls, floors or ceilings, only its plumbing: a forest of pipes that traces the missing houses, hung with white porcelain against the sky and taken over by water nymphs who now play in its streams.
textDetails: No one can say whether Armilla is unfinished or demolished, nor whether an enchantment or a mere whim is the cause.
It has no walls, no ceilings and no floors; only its water pipes make it look like a city at all.
The pipes rise vertically where the houses ought to be and branch horizontally where the floors ought to be.
It is a forest of pipes ending in taps, showers, spouts and overflows.
The white of a washbasin, a bathtub or some other porcelain stands out against the sky, likened to late fruit left hanging on the branches.
It seems the plumbers finished and left before the bricklayers came; or else the indestructible plumbing survived a catastrophe, an earthquake or the gnawing of termites.
Abandoned before or after it was lived in, it still cannot be called deserted.
Looking up among the pipes at any hour you may glimpse one or many young women, slender and not tall, lounging in bathtubs or arching under showers that hang over the void.
They wash, dry and perfume themselves, or comb their long hair in front of a mirror.
In the sun, the threads of water fanning from the showers glitter, together with the jets of the taps, the spurts, the splashes and the foam of sponges.
Marco's explanation: the water channelled through Armilla's pipes has stayed in the possession of nymphs and naiads.
Used to travelling along underground veins, they slipped easily into this new watery realm, bursting from many fountains and finding new mirrors, new games and new ways to enjoy the water.
Perhaps their invasion drove the humans out; or perhaps humans built Armilla as a votive offering to win over nymphs offended by the misuse of the waters.
They now seem content; in the mornings they can be heard singing.
Not in the text: the pipes' metal or colour, the number and height of the houses, or the ground; copper, the water-mirror floor and the scale are design choices.
visualConcept: An endless sheet of ankle-deep, perfectly still water, the city's own overflow, stretches into a pearly morning mist and mirrors everything; out of it rise low pale travertine foundation slabs, the only trace of the houses, and from the slabs grows a forest of copper pipes. The pipes follow an uncanny architectural logic: vertical risers stand at the corners and along the wall lines of houses that are not there, and at every storey height they branch into horizontal runs that cross the empty interiors like joists, so the eye assembles a whole town of two- to eight-storey houses drawn only in plumbing, with lanes and a small square between them. Along the branches sit elbows, tees and valve wheels, and every line ends in something useful: taps, shower roses on gooseneck arms, spouts, overflows, and a few open risers that burst upward like fountains. High up, at the levels of the missing bathrooms, glossy white porcelain hangs against the bright sky, claw-foot bathtubs, washbasins, cisterns and other fixtures, scattered through the copper branches like pale late fruit in a leafless orchard. Fine threads of water fan from the showers and pour from the taps, glittering in the low sun, with drifting foam and countless tiny rings where drops strike the mirror floor. Among the fixtures are the nymphs: small slender figures of pale translucent water-light with long flowing hair, lounging in tubs, arching under showers that hang over nothing, combing their hair at small oval mirrors fixed to the pipes, rendered as stylised refractive silhouettes, chaste and luminous, more water than body. There are no human figures anywhere: the city reads as an X-ray of its own water, inhabited only by the water's spirits.
layout: Ground: infinite still water plane at y=0 (planar reflection with a very light ripple normal), fading to mist at about 90 units. Town: within radius 12 of the origin, about 44 rectangular foundation slabs (footprints 1.2-2.4 by 1-2, raised 0.06 above the water) along two crossing lanes 1.2 wide, with a small square of radius 2.5 at the crossing and a few isolated slabs toward the edge. Storey height 0.5; most houses 2-6 storeys (pipe tops at 1-3 units), plus 4 tenement towers of 8 storeys (4 units). Pipes: per house 4-10 vertical risers (radius 0.018-0.03) at corners and along wall lines, horizontal runs at every storey around the perimeter and 1-3 across the interior; about 2500 straight segments plus instanced elbows, tees and crosses, and about 80 valve handwheels. Terminations: about 120 taps, 70 shower roses on gooseneck arms, 40 spouts, 30 overflows, and 8 rooftop risers acting as fountains (jets 0.6-1.2 high). Porcelain at true scale to a 0.25-unit person: about 40 claw-foot bathtubs (0.26 x 0.12 x 0.1), 70 washbasins (0.09 wide), 25 cisterns and other pieces on pipe brackets at storey heights, weighted toward the upper half of the town so they silhouette against the sky. Mirrors: 20 small oval mirrors (0.1 tall) on pipes beside basins. Nymphs: 18 figures about 0.22 tall (deliberately a little under the 0.25 standard), in tubs, under showers and at mirrors, mostly 1.5-4 units above the water. No humans.
signatureMotion: 1) Glittering water everywhere: each shower emits a fanned cone of fine bright streaks (GPU particles or scrolling line shaders) that catch the sun, taps pour thin twisting ribbons, overflows spurt in irregular pulses and rooftop risers fountain; drops landing on the mirror floor spawn expanding rings, and soap foam drifts and pops. 2) The nymphs live slowly in looping 6-12 s gestures (arching back under a shower, stretching in a tub, drawing a comb through long hair whose strands sway in a vertex shader); now and then one dissolves into a bright pulse that runs down through the pipes, under the water and up again to reappear at a shower across the town, as if travelling the underground veins. 3) The morning advances: the sun climbs slowly from the horizon so the sparkle sweeps from fixture to fixture, and faint motes drift upward in the warming air, a visual murmur of the morning singing.
interactionDescription: Fades in the ordinary town the plumbing implies: translucent plaster walls, floor slabs, roofs and dark window openings materialise exactly around the pipes (about 20 percent opacity with crisp edges), so the forest becomes a town of bathrooms and kitchens. As the rooms close in, the water threads stop, the porcelain disappears behind walls, the light flattens and the nymphs fade away, as if a human city and the nymphs' realm cannot occupy the same place. Toggle again and the walls dissolve upward like steam; the water returns first, then its tenants. The ghost town stays deliberately ambiguous: it could be the city that was never finished or the one that fell.
mood: Early morning, clear and fresh, the hour when the bathers sing: a low gold sun from the east rakes through the pipes and lights every thread of water; long thin shadows lie across the wet mirror floor; a pearly mist hangs at knee height and softens the horizon; the sky warms from peach at the rim to clear blue above. Serene, sensual and playful, everything glistening, with the hush of a bathhouse at dawn.
caption: Nothing in Armilla is a wall. Copper pipe sketches the missing houses, rising through absent rooms and branching across absent floors, and among its branches hang basins and bathtubs, white as fruit forgotten after the harvest. Whether the builders never came or the city fell away around its plumbing, the water stayed, and so did those who belong to water: slender bathers who sing in the morning above the void.
motto: Take away the walls, and the water still keeps house.
camera: Low and close, a pedestrian's upward glance: camera about 17 units from the town centre at a height of about 1.2 units, looking up to a target at (0, 2.2, 0), so the copper forest and its white porcelain stand against the bright morning sky while their reflections fill the lower frame; FOV about 38, slow drifting orbit. Allow pulling back to about 30 units to read the whole plan.
